chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from al-Mukhtār ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Mukhtār; and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Ḥasan al-ʿAlawī, all together from al-Fatḥ ibn Yazīd al-Jurjānī, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: concerning

About a man who entered another man’s house for theft or for lewdness, and the owner of the house killed him: is he to be killed in retaliation for him or not? He said: “Know that whoever enters another’s house, his blood has been rendered without protection, and nothing is due against him.”
Our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, said: I asked him

About a man who was violent toward his wife, or a woman who was violent toward her husband, and one of them killed the other. He said: “Nothing is upon them when they are deemed trustworthy; but if they are accused, he shall require them to swear by Allah that they did not intend killing.”

key_terms.أُهْدِرَ دَمُهُ: his blood is considered without legal protection
key_terms.مَأْمُونَيْنِ: regarded as trustworthy and not under suspicion

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a homeowner kills an intruder or if one spouse kills the other during a violent altercation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning liability for killing in two situations: when an intruder enters another’s house for theft or indecency, and when lethal harm occurs between spouses during violent altercation. It indicates the removal of liability in specific circumstances, while also requiring an oath when suspicion exists regarding intent to kill.
